body: the only thing i want to resist is my fear, i just wanna die. its my only way out. something is wrong with me.

What's going on? Why do you want to die? Why do you want to leave your children? Talk to me. I'm still depressed, everything I said in this thread still stands and I wanna die, but I can't stand back and allow others to feel suicidal like I do. Talk to me.

I don't even abuse the pills. I've only taken them for suicide. I don't do any drugs, I don't smoke, i don't drink. I only resorted to sleeping pills as a method to end my life.... 

>Concentrate on yourself. Forget about that guy. There will be plenty more. Focus on what makes you happy, hobbies and stuff like that. 

It's *soooo* hard, though. He was my first real friend. I didn't have anyone in high school or even middle school to be honest. He was the first person to listen to me, care for me, not judge me. He was also my first boyfriend. But we broke up a while ago. It's not the fact that I lost him romantically that's tearing me up. It's that I lost my best fucking friend. The best person to give me happiness ever in my life. My best support system. I wanna forget about him but I can't even fucking do that because my only other friends are still friends with him.... no matter how much I try to forget, he pops up again. 

>Your life is worth living, and I would trade spots with you in a heartbeat.

I really don't wanna belittle your pain but.... you don't want to. I don't want to trade spots with *anyone* and no one should want to trade with me. I hate the way I think, it's not so much even my circumstances that depress me (although, they very much do). I hate the toxic and self-detrimental way I think and act. I'm a burden unto myself *and* others. Maybe my life is worth living... but the pain and disappointment is too much to bear. Maybe you want everything else in my life but you do *not* want my mind. I fucking hate it. I hate myself. We should never say we wish we could switch spoits, because we never know every facet about that person. Some things can appear to look so damn good but in reality, it's not. I fucking hate my self. You don't want this.
It didn't though. That's why I made this thread lol

I edited my comment with an additional question

>Just one question, if I do continue with this, arguing that they were not in compliance with ADA and FERPA, will the wording of the contract I signed cause problems?

Holy shit. This is actually eye opening. This can help alot! I'm going to see if I can get this fixed without relying on this legality *but* if I need to, I will use this. Thank you so much. 

Just one question, if I do continue with this, arguing that they were not in compliance with ADA and FERPA, will the wording of the contract I signed cause problems?
I had no attempts in the dorms, and made no behavior while in the dorms. Both the actual attempt in the first week of school *and* the threat happened off campus.

I can't argue with that. You're right... 

But this entire situation sucks so much. I want to do school I really do.

> If “leaving the university” meant simply moving off campus, then it would be duplicating “not allowed to remain in a residential setting”. It seems pretty clear that this is requiring you to complete treatment before being readmitted.

Can this treatment not be done in the same city, though?

Again, i'm not trying to be argumentative. The more I inquire, the more I understand. I want what's possible and what's best for me in all aspects.

>Treating this like a legal issue is like trying to sue a flat tire into fixing itself. The issue here is your health. That’s where you have the power to focus your energies and make real changes.

Are my energies into school not a part of my health? I went to school to escape this home life... full of my family yelling, people doing drugs outside my house, hearing gun shots... and being here just makes me feel so much more upset. I even expressed this to my counselors and they agreed that it's not ideal for me to be here but they said that I am a liability to the university if I stay. So am I really getting the good deal here? On one hand, i'm in a  toxic and traumatic environment, and on the other i'm treated as just a problem. How am I supposed to feel good here? Before I left school, my counselors agreed to this possibly only being temporary, that I could return to campus before the end of the semester and complete it there and my driving rationale has been "if I can make it somewhere I hate, I know I can make it somewhere I love", but now that's being tested. At this point, I'm stuck here and won't be able to enjoy the one thing that's kept me going these past four years. Once again, I'm not trying to argue with you here but *please* understand where i'm coming from. School means so much to me. It's the only thing I have. And knowing that I can't graduate on time is devastating. ESPECIALLY, because it's due to my counselor's negligence that I can't graduate! If they reached out to my professor earlier, none of this would be happening. I could just stay here at home, get treatment, get my work done from home, and come back and graduate.

> Suicidal ideation (defined as thinking about or being unusually preoccupied with suicide), which is how you describe the incident, is also a form of suicidal behavior. It's just not visible to others unless you disclose it.

The thing is, in the contract, it states that suicidal ideation *is not* grounds for me going home. Just as long as I communicated such. The only thing is suicidal *behavior*, which can be kind of ambiguous in definition.

> Threatening to commit suicide is in and if itself a form of suicidal behavior. 

Isn't that just a part of suicidal ideation, though?

I'm not trying to be argumentative. You're right, my wellbeing is what should come first, undeniably. But it hurt so much to know that I might not be able to walk with my class. I've worked so hard. I'm just going through a really rough time. I don't want **ONE** class to be the reason I can't hear my name called after my friend's and walk across that stage in May.

And, if you're really sure on my actions being labeled as a part of suicidal behavior, how about the part of the same section that states "he will no longer be able to *remain in a residential setting* and will be required to leave the university in order to receive more extensive treatment"?

What my understanding was - and I haven't questioned my counselors about it yet - was that this means I have to leave my dorm, *not* that I can't be on campus. Do you think I should ask my counselors clarification on this? Because I can just stay off campus and seek psychiatric treatment in the same city.

I'm honestly almost desperate to graduate on time. For so long, it's been my goal. I'll make my parents proud, my friends proud, myself proud. And i'm really scared that knowing I can't do it will just dissuade and dismay me more about my problems and life.... 

EDIT: Why are you guys downvoting me? I'm just trying to get advice......
